newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Feb 25.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Feb 25.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The New South Wales Government's decision to build the multi-purpose Olympic velodrome in Bankstown rather than Liverpool has set back basketball club the West Sydney Slammers' bid to gain entry to the National Basketball League. Page 16.

The Australian Ericsson Cup national soccer league president Stefan Kamasz has warned Melbourne businessman Jack Dardalis that saving cash-strapped team the Collingwood Warriors won't be easy. Dardalis is putting together a A$1 million package to keep theside in competition next year. Page 17.

Australian Jockey Club Principal Club vice-chairman Ralph Lucas confirmed yesterday that racing code administrators discussed last week shutting down all forms of racing in the multi-billion dollar industry as a last resort bid to gain wagering tax relief from the New South Wales Government. Page 16.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Three members of the Australian Rugby Union team, prop Mark Hartill, five-eighth Tim Wallace and halfback Anthony Ekert have been left out of the 30-man New South Wales Super 12 squad. Selectors have relied upon current form and not past reputations by dropping several established players to make way for young talent. Page 42.

Australian sprinter Tony Marshall is upset that the results showing the finishing times of the Botany Bay Gift 120 metre handicap went missing after the race. Marshall lost the race on Sunday to former Olympic and world 100 metre champion Linford Christie by 0.01 of a second. Page 41.

The Australian Rugby League board has failed to punish North Sydney players accused of abusive behaviour towards elderly bowlers during a car park confrontation last week. The ARL declared the matter closed after taking a report on the incident from North president Ray Beattie. Page 42.
THE AGE

Australian fast bowler Anthony Stuart remains in high contention to join the touring Australian team in South Africa despite not playing in weeks due to an ankle injury. Stuart may be called in to the squad to replace injured bowler Paul Reiffel if he is orced to return home. Page C6.

Australian tennis player Todd Woodbridge said he had no answer to Michael Chang's court speed after losing the final of the St Jude Classic in Memphis on Monday. Woodbridge made a rash of unforced errors in losing to the top-seeded Chang 6-3, 6-4. Page C6

Australian pole-vaulter Emma George believes she can raise the world record again when she competes in the national championships this Friday. George set her 10th world record last Thursday when she cleared 4.55 metres at the Nike Track Classic. Page C6.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian Football Club Carlton is determined to promote young players in tomorrow night's Ansett Cup match against Melbourne at Waverley Park. Experienced Carlton players will be kept in cotton wool for the pre-season while Melbourne has a relatively setled squad. Page 72.

Australian golfer Greg Norman lost his top three position on the local money list after the Australasian PGA Tour ended last Sunday. Peter Senior's win at the Canon Challenge on the weekend lifted him to second place on the Order of Merit, pushing Norman own to fourth. Page 64.

Australian Commonwealth Games gold medallist marathon runner Steve Moneghetti is in doubt for Friday's 10 kilometre race at the national championships at Olympic Park due to an ankle injury. Moneghetti said he did not want to risk missing the World Cross Country Championships in Italy next month or the London Marathon in April. Page 70.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Rugby Union fans will be forced to pay A$60 dollars a ticket to watch Australia play Test matches against France and England this winter. The Australian Rugby Union blames the capacity of the Sydney Football Stadium for the ticket price. Page 68.

Control of the Australian administration of taekwondo has been taken over by the Australian Olympic Committee after the leaders of the sport were no longer recognised by the world governing body because of bitter factional fighting. Page 66.

The Australian Rugby League launched its 1997 premiership season at the Sydney Town Hall last night, confident of providing the best games every week of the season. ARL chief executive Neil Whittaker said he hoped an advertising campaign would encourage atendances from rival competition Super League. Page 64.
